title: Field scalar comparison for reflexive hulls and geometric prime divisors
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $Y$ be a geometrically integral geometrically normal finite-type $F$-scheme, and let $E/F$ be any field extension [def-weil-field, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-field-extension, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Geometrically normal means that all local rings remain integrally closed domains after every field extension. Put $Y_E=Y\times_F\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and let $p:Y_E\to Y$ be the projection. Use the coherent duals, reflexive hulls and divisorial sheaves $\mathcal O(D)$ of [lem-sfb-normal-divisorial-open-restriction] and tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every coherent module $M$ [pqf-def-coherent], the canonical comparison $p^*(M^\vee)\to(p^*M)^\vee$ is an isomorphism, and hence $p^*(M^{**})\cong(p^*M)^{**}$ compatibly with evaluation. In particular pullback preserves coherent reflexive rank-one modules and commutes with the reflexive tensor product $(M\otimes N)^{**}$ of such modules.

Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_s$ be distinct geometrically integral prime divisors on $Y$, with their reduced structures. Then $(Z_i)_E$ are distinct reduced integral prime divisors on $Y_E$. For any integers $n_i$, put $D=\sum_i n_i[Z_i]$ and $D_E=\sum_i n_i[(Z_i)_E]$. There is a canonical isomorphism $p^*\mathcal O_Y(D)\cong\mathcal O_{Y_E}(D_E)$, compatible with the inclusions in the rational-function sheaves and with restriction to opens. No separability, algebraicity or finiteness of $E/F$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-assembled scalar comparison: Tag 0EBF (divisors-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive), Tag 0EB9 (more-algebra-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive); the dual comparison is the finite-presentation kernel calculation: present M by finite free modules and tensor the kernel defining Hom, using flatness; Tag 0EBM (divisors-lemma-normal-class-group) and Tag 0EBJ (divisors-lemma-reflexive-S2-extend). For geometric prime divisors compare their Cartier equations outside codimension two; algebra.tex Tag 00P3 (lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension) preserves the discarded codimension. These tags are supporting ingredients, not an assertion that one tag states this exact assembled comparison.

proof.text: Work on affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ in a finite affine cover of $Y$, whose inverse images are $W_E=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A\otimes_FE$. The rings $A,B$ are finite-type algebras over fields, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a field has only two ideals). All their localizations are Noetherian: an ideal in a localization is generated by the images of generators of its contraction. Geometric integrality [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] makes both rings domains. They are normal by the assumed normality of every scalar extension: an element of the fraction field integral over an affine ring lies in each local ring; its denominator ideal cannot lie in any maximal ideal, so it lies in the affine ring. The map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. Coherent sheaves are quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], and have finite affine section modules by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine].

source.place: Tags 00FN (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00HI (algebra-lemma-flat-base-change); affine setup for Tags 0EBF and 0EBM.

proof.text: For $M$ coherent, choose a local finite presentation $\mathcal O^a\to\mathcal O^b\to M\to0$. Such a presentation exists by the finite-presentation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] on the Noetherian affine section modules of Step 1. By the definition [def-pur-sheaf-hom], $M^\vee$ is the kernel of the transposed map $\mathcal O^b\to\mathcal O^a$: a functional on the cokernel is precisely a functional annihilating the relations. Its affine module is therefore $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M(W),A)$. This is finite by [lem-pc-noetherian-finite-kernels-cokernels]. The same kernel description on basic opens, or the Hom comparison for localization in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented], identifies this sheaf with the associated module sheaf. Under tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], the local presentation becomes $\mathcal O_{W_E}^a\to\mathcal O_{W_E}^b\to p^*M\to0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] the pullback of the associated sheaf of an $A$-module $P$ on $W$ is the associated sheaf of $B\otimes_AP$ on $W_E$, with $1\otimes m$ corresponding to the pullback of $m$; this applies to $P=M(W)$ and $P=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M(W),A)$. Apply the same Hom-comparison node with $R=A$, $R'=B$, $N=A$. It gives exactly $\theta_M:p^*(M^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}(p^*M)^\vee$, taking $b\otimes\lambda$ to $(b'\otimes m\mapsto bb'\lambda(m))$. These are the canonical comparisons, so the local isomorphisms agree on overlaps.

source.place: Tag 087R (more-algebra-lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext), part (1); finite-free kernel calculation for coherent sheaf duals.

proof.text: Step 2 also proves coherence of $M^\vee$, so apply it again to obtain $\alpha_M=(\theta_M^\vee)^{-1}\theta_{M^\vee}:p^*M^{**}\xrightarrow{\sim}(p^*M)^{**}$. Evaluation commutes with this comparison: on $b\otimes m$ paired with $b'\otimes\lambda$ both routes give $bb'\lambda(m)$. Thus if evaluation for $M$ is invertible, so is evaluation for $p^*M$. Finite generation survives tensoring by carrying a finite set of generators to $1\otimes m_i$, hence pullback is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. If $M$ has rank one, tensor its generic isomorphism $M\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}A\simeq\operatorname{Frac}A$ with $\operatorname{Frac}B$; its pullback has rank one. Finally the balanced-tensor formula $(b\otimes m)\otimes(b'\otimes n)\mapsto bb'\otimes(m\otimes n)$ and its inverse identify pullback of a tensor with the tensor of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply $\alpha$ to $M\otimes N$. The reflexive rank-one tensor assertion on both normal schemes follows from [lem-sfb-normal-divisorial-open-restriction].

source.place: Tags 0EBF (divisors-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive) and 0EBL (divisors-lemma-reflexive-normal); canonical evaluation and tensor formulas written out.

proof.text: Fix a divisor $Z_i$ meeting $W$, with prime ideal $\mathfrak p_i\subset A$. Flat exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] gives $0\to B\otimes_A\mathfrak p_i\to B\to (A/\mathfrak p_i)\otimes_FE\to0$, with image $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak p_iB$. The last ring is a domain by geometric integrality of $Z_i$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Hence the scheme-theoretic inverse image is reduced and integral on every such affine, and globally integral by that same definition. Moreover $A/\mathfrak p_i\to(A/\mathfrak p_i)\otimes_FE$ is injective (tensoring a nonzero vector with $1$ is injective, extend $1\in E$ to an $F$-basis), so $\mathfrak q_i\cap A=\mathfrak p_i$. Distinct divisors therefore stay distinct: equal inverse images would give equal contracted ideals on every affine open. This includes affines missing $Z_i$, where its ideal is the unit ideal.

source.place: Tag 0EBM (divisors-lemma-normal-class-group), prime ideals underlying the construction; affine scalar extension and geometric integrality.

proof.text: For a nonempty $Z_i\cap W$, write $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_i$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pB$. The ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a DVR by [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices]; choose a uniformizer $t\in A_{\mathfrak p}$. Since $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p$, there is a map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$. Its image of $t$ generates $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, because this ideal is generated by the image of $\mathfrak p$. Put $R=B_{\mathfrak q}$. The image of $t$ is nonzero, since $A\to B$ and localization into their fraction fields are injective. The quotient $R/(t)$ is the residue field and has dimension zero. The maximal ideal of $R$ has height $\dim R$: its chains are all the prime chains of this local ring, as in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. Apply [lem-sc-principal-quotient-dimension-full-height] to $R,t$ and its maximal ideal. Its Noetherian, nonzerodivisor, containment and full-height hypotheses have just been checked, and it gives $\dim R=0+1=1$. Thus $(Z_i)_E$ is a prime divisor. Its DVR maximal ideal is generated by the image of $t$, so the normalized valuation of that image is exactly one, with no ramification multiplicity.

source.place: Tag 00KW (algebra-lemma-one-equation), applied to the local ring at the extended prime; Tag 0EBM prime-divisor local equations.

proof.text: Use the fractional lattices $I_A(H)$ of [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices], whose sign is $I_A(H)=\mathcal O(-H)(W)$. For a height-one prime $\mathfrak p$, $I_A([\mathfrak p])=\mathfrak p$: the other nonnegative valuation conditions put an element in $A=\bigcap A_{\mathfrak r}$, and its positive $\mathfrak p$-valuation means that it belongs to $\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}\cap A=\mathfrak p$. The same calculation holds over $B$ for the height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ from Step 5. By Step 4, tensoring the inclusion of this ideal identifies $B\otimes_A I_A([\mathfrak p])$ with $\mathfrak pB=\mathfrak q=I_B([\mathfrak q])$. Thus the comparison for $\mathcal O(-Z_i)$ is an equality of the embedded fractional modules, not just an abstract isomorphism. It glues by the localization assertion of the lattice node; outside $Z_i$ both ideals are the structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0EBM (divisors-lemma-normal-class-group), embedded negative prime-divisor modules; Tag 0AVB (more-algebra-lemma-reflexive-over-normal), intersection characterization.

proof.text: For a nonzero finite fractional module $J\subset K=\operatorname{Frac}A$, every map $J\to A$ is multiplication by a unique element of $K$: extend to $K$, where $J\otimes_AK=K$. Hence $J^\vee=\{f\in K:fJ\subset A\}$. For $J=I_A(H)$ the height-one localization formulas and $A=\bigcap A_{\mathfrak r}$ of [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices] give $J^\vee=I_A(-H)$. Thus dualizing Step 6 with Step 2 proves the required embedded comparison for $\mathcal O(Z_i)$ as well. More generally multiplication gives the canonical reflexive tensor identification for divisorial sheaves in [lem-sfb-normal-divisorial-open-restriction]: after localizing at any height-one prime it multiplies the principal lattices $t^{-a}A_{\mathfrak r}$ and $t^{-b}A_{\mathfrak r}$ into $t^{-(a+b)}A_{\mathfrak r}$. Double duals localize by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented], and are reflexive by [lem-sfb-coherent-reflexive-hull]; the fractional-lattice intersection characterization then identifies this double dual with $\mathcal O(H+H')$ inside $K$. Express $D$ as a sum of signed copies of the finitely many $Z_i$, and apply these identities and the tensor comparison of Step 3 successively. This proves $p^*\mathcal O(D)\simeq\mathcal O(D_E)$ for all integers $n_i$; zero copies give $\mathcal O(0)=\mathcal O$.

source.place: Tags 0EBL (divisors-lemma-reflexive-normal), 0EBM (divisors-lemma-normal-class-group), 0AY4 (divisors-lemma-dual-reflexive); canonical multiplication of fractional modules.

proof.text: On each affine, every map constructed above sends $b\otimes f$ to $b\,p(f)$ in $\operatorname{Frac}B$. For duals this follows from the multiplication description in Step 7; for tensors it is the displayed balanced formula in Step 3. Thus these maps commute with the inclusions into the rational-function sheaves. The localizations of [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices] and the restriction assertion of [lem-sfb-normal-divisorial-open-restriction] show that the maps agree on each basic-open restriction and hence glue and commute with restriction to every open. No equality $E\otimes_F k(Y)=k(Y_E)$ is used: only its natural map to $k(Y_E)$ and multiplication there. Each construction uses field flatness and geometric integrality or normality as stated, so no algebraicity, separability or finite-degree hypothesis on $E/F$ has entered.
